raw_final_content:
The bird is a medium-sized gray-brown arboreal passerine with a fairly slender bill, a moderately long tail and pale underparts that look mottled or streaked. The first and third frames are consistent with one bird; the second is mostly a wide context view.

Brown-eared Bulbul, Hypsipetes amaurotis (ヒヨドリ), is my leading species candidate: the body proportions, bill, overall gray-brown tone and underpart pattern fit well. However, the images are digitally enlarged/soft, and I cannot cleanly resolve the brown ear-coverts patch or a diagnostic crest. Because the benchmark intentionally withholds geography, I would record Hypsipetes sp. at medium confidence and keep H. amaurotis as the leading species candidate rather than call it high-confidence species.

A sharp lateral head image, full tail/wing view or a short call recording would resolve much of the remaining uncertainty.
